newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Philadelphia Bank revenues soar in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Philadelphia Bank revenues soar in 1996.

text.p: Jordan's Philadelphia Investment Bank revenues rose a sharp 117 percent to 2.2 million dinars in 1996, buoyed by expanded commercial banking operations, its general manager said on Tuesday.
He declined to give a figure for 1996 profits, but said the bank had secured commitments to double its capital and expected it to turn around recent losses stemming from bad debts.

"Our healthy results in 1996 were because we focused on the work in which real profits come from, the commercial and investment side," Nimer Shakaa, general manager of Philadelphia Investment Bank, told Reuters.
Shakaa said 43 percent of net revenues in 1996 came from expanded commercial activities including commissions, fees, and trade finance. Philadelphia Bank's revenues stood at 1,013,000 dinars in 1995.

Shakaa said the bank had already secured commitments to cover a two-stage doubling of its capital to 20 million dinars by end of June, in line with a Central Bank ruling for Jordanian banks to reach a minimum 20 dinar capital ceiling.

Shakaa said private investors and existing shareholders had already covered a first stage seven million dinar private placement, which will raise the bank's capital to 17 million dinars by end of January. Another three million will be covered in a private placement by mid-June.
He said he was confident the bank would be put on a healthy footing and clear a legacy of bad debts.

The bank which came into being in 1993 from a merger of two finance and real estate firms, Jordan Finance House for Development and Investment and Darco Company for Investment and Housing, inherited some of their debts.
Bank officials say leading Arab investors were amongst the new shareholders of the bank.
Asked about 1996 earnings outlook, Shakaa declined to give figures but said "they would definitely be better in 1996."
The bank's losses fell sharply to 441,000 dinars at end June 1996 from 754,000 dinars in the previous period.

Bank officials say the bank is expected to show much lower losses in 1996 even after taking large provisions for bad debts and revaluation of stock. They forecast the bank would record profits in 1997.
Philadelphia Bank's total assets stood at 59 million dinars and its customer deposits at 34.6 million dinars in mid June 1996.
